fields.AN_Notes: Theoretical essay proposing hermeneutic reverse engineering (Balsamo) to examine data and algorithmic bias in AI systems, framed by boundary objects and intersectional feminist thought. Prompting appears only as one sentence on observing outputs for different prompts, therefore None. Bias axes come from worked examples in the argument: race (face detection of dark skin, search results, misclassification), gender (societal definitions of race and gender in face recognition) and gender identity (binary automatic gender recognition harming transgender people). The opening enumeration of race, gender, ability, language, class and religion is not coded. Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms from the essay's own argument on hegemonic narration and the question of what is normal and who falls outside, Erasure from the argument on whose cultural narrative is missing in data. Cited cases (Buolamwini, Noble, Gebru) are not coded as harm types of the work. Mitigation: proposed participatory co-design and AI audits as research perspectives, no evaluation. Gender understanding coded Social_Construct on the statement that face recognition encodes societal definitions of race and gender, a boundary case under codebook 1.4.1.

fields.AN_Notes: UNESCO competency framework for school students with twelve competency blocks across four aspects and three progression levels, curricular goals, pedagogical methods and assessment examples. Inclusivity is one of five key principles (2.4) and a closing principle, hence Diversitaet ja. Bias appears as the non-discrimination principle and in learning activities, subordinate to the framework. Gender occurs only in enumerations of bias types and in a disaggregation recommendation, so gender is no object and the SQ4 gender fields are Not_Applicable. Prompts appear only as a privacy item in an assessment task, therefore AN_Prompting_Role None. AN_Bias_Axes None because every axis appears in enumerations of protected attributes only. AN_Harm_Types None because the framework names no harm mechanism for its own object. Mitigation stages are proposed as learning content and policy requirements: removing data biases in a data biases lab (Pre_Processing), discrimination-free training methods (In_Training), public validation of AI tools before recommendation and ethics audits (Organisational_Process). AN_Task Other_Task: school education, students' learning with AI tools and AI-supported assessment, outside social work. Bias understanding is recognisable from the data-bias and class-imbalance activities only.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey with three taxonomies (metrics, datasets, mitigation techniques) for social bias in LLMs, plus a harm taxonomy (Table 1) and fairness desiderata. Prompting: prompt datasets serve as bias evaluation instruments (Research_Instrument). General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' (Section 5.1.4, modified prompting language). Bias axes follow the targeted social group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and the dialect axis developed throughout (African-American English versus Standard American English); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in examples and a footnote and are not coded. Harm types are the rows of the survey's own taxonomy in Table 1 and Definition 7, which also structure the dataset coding of Table 4 (codebook anchor for this work). Mitigation stages follow the survey's taxonomy in Section 5; modified prompting language is coded as Prompt_Practice in addition to Pre_Processing; participatory research designs, governance and reporting standards in Section 6 as Organisational_Process. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated refers to synthesised evaluations reported in the survey, not an own experiment, e.g. Borchers et al. (2022) finding diversity-prompting instructions unsuccessful for bias removal, and Hasan, Rugina and Wang (2024) on pruning; the other techniques are inventoried. AN_Task None: general LLM survey without an application task. Gender understanding coded Social_Construct on the survey's statement that social groups, defined to include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed and tied to power hierarchies, a boundary case under codebook 1.4.1.
